mcqs.q: Using A=1, B=2, C=3, D=4 …, write the word “BAD” as numbers.
mcqs.e: B=2, A=1, D=4, so BAD = 2 1 4. Letters can be encoded as numbers.

mcqs.q: A robot reaches a dead-end while trying to get through a maze. The smart thing to do is…
o: try the exact same path again
go back and try a different path
mcqs.e: Backing up and trying another path is the seed of search - try, check, try again.

mcqs.q: Which AI can make a NEW picture when you describe it in words?
mcqs.e: An image generator is generative AI that draws a brand-new picture from your words; the others only show or change pictures that already exist.

mcqs.q: How does an AI learn to know what a cat looks like?
o: It asks a real cat itself
It looks at many cat pictures
mcqs.e: AI learns from lots of examples (called data). Many cat pictures help it learn cats.

mcqs.q: A chatbot builds a whole sentence by…
o: copying a full page from a book
adding the most likely next word, again and again
mcqs.e: Generating text = repeatedly guessing the next word - a “what comes next?” game.

mcqs.q: Find the repeating rule, then say what colour the 8th bead is.
mcqs.byhand: ①🔴 ②🟡 ③🔵 ④🔴 ⑤🟡 ⑥🔵 ⑦❓ ⑧❓
mcqs.e: The rule repeats every 3 beads: red, yellow, blue. The 7th starts a new group (red), so the 8th is yellow. Finding the repeating unit lets you predict any position, not just the next.

mcqs.q: Should you tell a chatbot your home address and phone number?
o: Yes, so it can help you better
No, keep private things to yourself
Only if a friend tells you to
mcqs.e: Keep private information safe. Never share your address, phone number or passwords with a chatbot.

mcqs.q: A chatbot sometimes says something that is NOT true. What should you do?
o: Believe it because computers are clever
Use it in your homework anyway
Share it with all your friends
Check it with a trusted grown-up
mcqs.e: AI can make mistakes. Always check important things with a trusted person or source.

mcqs.q: Which of these can AI NOT really do?
mcqs.e: AI has no real feelings. It can use the word “happy,” but it does not feel.

mcqs.q: To help an AI sort photos into “dog” and “not a dog,” we are teaching it to…
mcqs.e: Putting things into groups like dog / not-a-dog is called classifying.

mcqs.q: Your friend asks you to use AI to write their homework and pretend they did it. Is that fair?
o: Yes, it saves a lot of time
Yes, if the work looks neat
mcqs.e: Pretending AI’s work is your own is not honest. AI can help you learn, but the work should be yours.

mcqs.q: A video app keeps showing you more cat videos after you watch one. What is it doing?
o: deleting the videos you skip past
copying videos straight from your friends
learning what you like and suggesting more of it
mcqs.e: A recommendation system learns from what you watch and suggests similar things, handy, but it can trap you in a bubble.

mcqs.q: Inside a computer, a photo is really stored as…
o: a single letter of the alphabet
the name of its main colour
a tiny copy of the real scene
mcqs.e: Computers store pictures (and words) as numbers, not paint or letters.

mcqs.q: If an AI only ever saw RED apples, what might it get wrong?
o: It will refuse to look at apples
It will recognise every kind of fruit
It might think all apples are red
It will always give correct answers
mcqs.e: If the examples are not fair and varied, the AI learns a biased idea - here, that all apples are red.

mcqs.q: What is a good way to use generative AI for your ideas?
o: Let it do all the thinking for you
Use it only to play games
Use it for ideas, then think too
mcqs.e: AI can help you brainstorm, but you should still use your own brain and check the ideas.

mcqs.q: To get good help from an AI assistant, the best way to ask is…
o: in as few words as you can
clearly, saying exactly what you want
by repeating it many times over
mcqs.e: Asking clearly and kindly is the seed of good prompting.

mcqs.q: Who makes AI programs?
o: They come already inside every computer
mcqs.e: People design and build AI. That means people are responsible for using it well.

mcqs.q: Be the robot and follow the rule exactly: “IF a word starts with S, THEN put it in the STAR box; OTHERWISE put it in the MOON box.” Where do the words “sun” and “cat” go?
o: sun → STAR box, cat → MOON box
sun → MOON box, cat → STAR box
mcqs.e: “sun” starts with S, so it goes in the STAR box; “cat” does not, so it goes in the MOON box. Following a rule exactly, step by step, is just what a computer does.

mcqs.q: Which task is generative AI BEST at helping with?
mcqs.e: Generative AI is good at making drafts of writing or pictures for you to improve. It cannot read your mind or know live facts on its own.

mcqs.q: A helper robot wants to water a thirsty plant. Which step comes FIRST in its helper loop?
o: check if the soil is dry
decide how much water to pour
wait for a person to say go
mcqs.e: A helper works in a loop: Sense → Think → Act. It must sense (check the soil) first, before deciding and acting.

structured.title: Task 1 · Be the Sorting Robot
structured.scenario:
A robot sorts fruit using only two rules:
• Rule 1: IF the fruit is yellow, THEN put it in Basket A.
• Rule 2: IF the fruit is red, THEN put it in Basket B.

The fruits are: 🍌 banana (yellow), 🍎 apple (red), 🍋 lemon (yellow), 🍓 strawberry (red), 🍏 green apple (green).
parts: a) For each fruit, write which basket it goes in. (Be the robot - follow the rules exactly.)
b) The green apple does not match any rule. What should the robot do? Explain your idea.
c) Why does a robot need clear rules to do its job well?

model.text: Banana → Basket A · Lemon → Basket A · Apple → Basket B · Strawberry → Basket B. (2 marks each correct match.)
model.rationale: Rewards following an algorithm step by step, exactly as written - the heart of how computers run rules.

model.text: Any sensible answer: the robot should NOT guess and throw it away. It could leave it aside, ask a person, or a new rule could be added (e.g., “IF green, THEN Basket C”).
model.rationale: Shows the child understands that AI fails safely when it meets something outside its rules, instead of pretending to know.

model.text: Clear rules let the robot make the same correct choice every time and not get confused. Without rules it would not know what to do.
model.rationale: Introduces the idea that AI behaviour comes from its instructions/data - a first step toward understanding bias and error.

structured.totalNote: Full marks need correct sorting (a), a safe idea for the unknown fruit (b), and a reason rules matter (c).

structured.title: Task 2 · Design a Helper Robot (AI Agent)
structured.scenario:
An AI agent is a helper that can do three things by itself to reach a goal:
SENSE (look or listen) → THINK (decide what to do) → ACT (do something).

Imagine a friendly helper robot for your classroom whose goal is to keep the classroom tidy.
parts: a) Draw or describe your helper robot. What can it sense (see/hear)?
b) Write its three steps for tidying up: SENSE → THINK → ACT.
c) Think carefully: Your robot sees a drawing lying on the floor. It is told to throw away rubbish, but this might be someone’s special artwork. What should the robot do, and why?

model.text: Any clear robot with at least one way to sense - e.g., “eyes/camera to see the floor,” “ears to hear instructions.”
model.rationale: Checks the child grasps that an agent needs input from the world before it can act.

model.text: SENSE: sees a toy/paper on the floor. THINK: decides it is out of place and where it belongs. ACT: picks it up and puts it in the right spot. (3 marks per stage.)
model.rationale: The sense→think→act loop is the core idea of an agent; marks reward all three stages, not just ‘a robot that cleans’.

model.text: The robot should NOT just throw it away. It should pause and check or ask a person first (“Is this rubbish or something you want to keep?”), because it could be someone’s treasured work.
model.rationale: A real dilemma: following an order vs. respecting people. Good answers show the agent should ask when unsure rather than cause harm - an early lesson in AI acting responsibly.

structured.totalNote: Award up to full marks for a clear agent (a), a complete sense→think→act loop (b), and a kind, careful choice with a reason (c).
